script.base: Spread, total, and moneyline were not saved, so this is form-only and the book’s expected leader and point total are unknown. Through weeks 1-2 MIN has been a Jones run game (35 carries, 145 yards) plus a Jefferson pass game (16 targets, 147 yards), while TB has been an Irving game (25 carries, 134 yards, and 11 targets at -47 air yards). Base flow is competitive: MIN keeps feeding Jones but into a TB run defense at 3.26 YPC, and MIN’s 78% blitz pushes TB toward Irving checkdowns rather than the deep air to Egbuka (159) and Hurst (179).
script.flip1: TB leads and clocks it. MIN abandons the 35-carry Jones lean, Addison’s 7-target share rises behind Jefferson, and Irving’s receiving work dries up because TB no longer needs the blitz outlet.
script.flip2: Shootout. Both passing games spike, Addison converts the 70 air yards and Egbuka converts the 159 air yards, and the quiet-WR under dies even if Irving’s checkdowns also cash.

data_check.notes: No model, sim median, or Pinnacle no-vig is in the pack, so step 8 cannot size a price gap; that is missing, not a contradiction. Addison’s 21 yards on 7 targets is 10.5 per game versus 36.5. His 70 air yards are unconverted opportunity, not a yardage total that already clears 36.5, so they are a kill risk rather than a contradicting result. Irving’s 49 yards on 11 targets is 24.5 per game versus 16.5, and the -47 air yards agree with a short over into a 78% blitz. Jones 145 rush yards on 35 carries was not selected: at TB’s 3.26 YPC, 17.5 carries projects about 57, only a few yards over 52.5, with Mason already at 15 carries. Egbuka’s 79 yards on 11 targets (39.5 per game) sits closer to 49.5 and carries 159 air yards, so Addison is the cleaner under.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both lost because the two-game roles did not travel. TB’s middle, 12.4 YPA on 10 throws, was the soft spot, Jefferson drew the extra attention, and Addison turned the 70 air yards into one 30-yard catch to clear 36.5. Separately MIN did not blitz near 78%, TB stayed on schedule with Irving’s 5.36 rush YPC, and the 11 targets at -47 air yards were a negative-script artifact, so he finished with one short screen under 10 yards. A late Irving or Addison snap limit would have caused the same miss, and this pack had no injury report to catch it.
slip_story: One non-shootout story: MIN’s throws stay concentrated on Jefferson’s 16-target role so Addison’s 7-target, 21-yard role stays under 36.5, and MIN’s 78% blitz keeps TB in quick answers so Irving’s checkdown receiving clears 16.5. Not a Jones clock-grind stack and not an Egbuka/Hurst deep stack. Both legs fail together if TB leads, MIN is forced into a pass-heavy comeback, and TB runs the clock.
